subject: PulsePay payment-api: sudden p95 latency + qps drop — triage / rollback request
messages:
From: Andrew Moss <andrew@pulsepay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-01 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Payment API latency spike — urgent

Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp degradation on our payment enrichment endpoint around 07:05 PT — p95 jumped from ~420ms to ~3.8s and sustained; overall request throughput for our integrated routes dropped ~40%. This started right after your scheduled runtime push at 06:45 (per your status page). Impact: payment processing queues are backing up and some customer flows are timing out.

Attached are a few traces from our side (span ids + request ids). Can you confirm whether any kernel/quantization changes were included in today’s push? We need an ETA on a fix or mitigation; our internal on-call is holding here and we need a plan we can communicate to operations.

Thanks,
Andrew Moss
CTO, PulsePay
attachments: pulsepay_perf_trace_20280601.zip

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-01 08:20:12 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Payment API latency spike — urgent

Forwarding Andrew’s note. TL;DR: PulsePay p95 ~3.8s, qps -40%. Spike coincides with 06:45 runtime push (kernel scheduling + new quant path). Requesting immediate triage and a product decision on a canary rollback if SRE confirms correlation. Proposed immediate actions:

- Ben: please validate whether the 06:45 change introduced the altered kernel scheduling path for multi-tenant gen-api (particularly on a2/g5 instances). Check KV cache hit rates and any sudden cache evictions.
- SRE: if correlation is strong, can we temporarily route PulsePay traffic to dedicated pool / older runtime image to stop the customer impact?
- Product (Marissa, Laura): if routing to older runtime helps, we’ll need sign-off on a short-term canary rollback for PulsePay only (no org-wide rollback) and a customer note. Also need a roadmap ask: prioritize an explicit KV-warmup mechanism for pinned sessions.

I’ve attached the traces Andrew sent. Please ack and give first-response ETA by 08:40.

— Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-01 08:33:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Payment API latency spike — urgent

Ack — investigating. Quick notes from initial checks (08:30):
- The 06:45 rollout included a change to the kernel selection heuristics and enabled a new quantized execution path for certain attention patterns.
- For PulsePay tenant traffic we see a sudden increase in KV misses and a matching rise in cold-started attention kernels (roughly 1.6x).
- We’ve temporarily increased dedicated pool capacity for PulsePay (scaled +30%) and applied a routing rule to prefer older runtime image (image:v202805_legacy) for their tenant id — this reduced observed p95 to ~950ms in preliminary tests.

Short-term ask: if Product okays, we can maintain the routing rule for PulsePay and schedule a tenant-scoped rollback of the runtime change. We recommend keeping the routing for 2-4 hours while we validate.

I’m attaching server-side KV stats dump and sample heap logs (kv-warmup-samples.log).

— Ben
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: kv-warmup-samples.log

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-01 09:02:58 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Payment API latency spike — urgent

Thanks, team — good work triaging quickly. A few product asks before we proceed with a tenant rollback:

1) Impact analysis: we need clear measurements of any quality delta between legacy image and v202806 runtime for PulsePay’s common prompt shapes. Laura, can you run a small batch eval (100 representative requests) vs both images in the next 45 minutes and surface token-level diffs?

2) Customer messaging: Evelyn/PR — we should send a concise ops note to PulsePay that describes the mitigation and the expected customer experience. Draft below — please edit:  

--- draft customer note ---
Subject: Short-term mitigation for elevated latency on Payment enrichment
Hi Andrew / PulsePay Ops,
We deployed a targeted mitigation at 08:25 PT that routes your tenant to a prior runtime image. In our tests this has reduced p95 from ~3.8s to ~950ms. We will keep this routing in place while we validate. Next steps: 1) we will run additional diff checks to ensure no quality regressions; 2) if all looks good we will schedule a tenant-scoped rollback of the runtime change and share a timeline; 3) longer term we will prioritize a KV-warmup feature to avoid cold-start regressions for pinned sessions.
Estimated time to resolution: 2–6 hours.
Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success
--- end draft ---

3) Roadmap ask: Priyom, please capture a short ticket to prioritize an automatic KV-warmup for pinned sessions + a telemetry flag to detect when quantized path increases cold kernel starts. We’ll consider accelerating this to the next sprint.

If the eval shows negligible quality delta, I approve keeping the tenant routing + a tenant rollback (timebox 4 hours). Otherwise we need a different mitigation.

— Marissa
VP, Product — Runtime

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Moss <andrew@pulsepay.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-01 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment API latency spike — urgent

Andrew — quick update for PulsePay ops: 

1) We have applied a tenant-scoped routing rule that sends your traffic to our prior runtime image (image:v202805_legacy). Early measurements show p95 reduced to ~950ms; throughput is recovering.
2) Our SRE and runtime teams are running a focused eval to compare output quality between the two images. We expect results within ~60 minutes.
3) Next steps we’re pursuing in parallel: short tenant rollback (if eval passes), and a prioritized ticket to add an explicit KV warmup and telemetry for quantized-path cold starts.

We recommend keeping the routing rule in place for the next 2–4 hours while we validate. We’ll send another update at ~13:10 PT or sooner if things change.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll treat this as a post-incident action item with clear owners and timelines. If you’d like a quick call, we can spin up a 15-min bridge.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

--- proposed follow-up actions (internal) ---
- Ben: maintain routing + continue telemetry collection (owner)
- Laura: run 100-request diff eval vs both images and post results to INF-7812 (owner, 09:20)
- Priyom: create INF-7812 subtask for KV warmup + telemetry (owner)
- Evelyn/Marissa: approve tenant rollback if diffs are within acceptable bounds (owner)
